chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Aban, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayabah and Abu al-'Abbas, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

If you do not know whether you have prayed three or four, and your judgment falls upon three, then build upon three. And if your judgment falls upon four, then say the salam and leave. And if your doubt is evenly balanced, then leave and pray two rak'ahs while you are sitting.

key_terms.أَرْبَعًا: four rak'ahs in the prayer under doubt
key_terms.ثَلَاثًا: three rak'ahs in the prayer under doubt
key_terms.رَأْيُكَ: your considered judgment or stronger assessment
key_terms.فَابْنِ عَلَى الثَّلَاثِ: proceed on the basis that three rak'ahs have been prayed

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they doubt whether they prayed three or four rak'ahs?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling for doubt in salat (prayer) between three and four rak'ahs. If one’s stronger judgment favors three, one proceeds on that basis; if it favors four, one completes the prayer; and if the doubt is equal, one performs two seated rak'ahs after ending the prayer.
